candidates.tagline: EU paid €30M for traffic cameras. Moscow got 279 new spy posts.
candidates.story: Slovakia installed 279 NERO R-ONE speed cameras using EU road-safety funds, then its national security service discovered they were rebranded Russian gear with SMS-triggered backdoor shell access and passwordless live video feeds.
candidates.why_funny: A government scheme to make roads safer accidentally handed Russia a ready-to-activate nationwide surveillance network—reachable by a text from a St Petersburg phone number.
candidates.alt: A grey traffic speed-enforcement camera mounted on a roadside pole, trees in the background

candidates.tagline: New messaging app delivers texts by pigeon. LA→NYC: 22 hrs. Bird may die.
candidates.story: Developer Noah Iarrobino launched Carrier Pidge, an iOS app that sends messages via virtual carrier pigeon at 110 mph real-world distance — a cross-country text takes 22 hours to arrive, and there is a 0.2% chance the pigeon dies en route.
candidates.why_funny: The developer openly describes the app as having 'genuinely no practical use', yet it went viral as the logical endpoint of inbox-fatigue culture.
candidates.alt: Close-up portrait of a pigeon strutting across sandy ground, looking directly ahead
